positives: If this company sold everything it owns and paid off everything it owes, there would be real money left over. It owns more than it owes.
It hasn't borrowed too much money - what it owes is less than what the business itself is worth.
It has plenty of cash and other easy-to-sell things on hand - more than twice enough to cover the bills it owes over the next year.
worries: Counting all the money it uses to run the business, it isn't making any profit right now.

This business makes less profit on the money it uses than that money actually costs to raise. That usually means competitors aren't held back from doing the same thing it does - no real moat protecting it.

qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal year 2025, Moderna reported total revenue of $1.9 billion, down from $3.2 billion in 2024, primarily due to a 42% decline in net COVID vaccine sales; net loss was $2.8 billion, narrower than 2024's $3.6 billion loss. The company now has three commercial products (Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE, and mRESVIA) and highlighted 2025 developments including the U.S. launch of mNEXSPIKE, expansion of U.S. and international (UK, Canada, Australia) manufacturing capacity, a new $1.5 billion five-year credit facility, and pipeline progress in oncology (intismeran autogene with Merck), rare disease (propionic acidemia collaboration with Recordati), and infectious disease (flu, flu+COVID, norovirus candidates).

qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes a 'broad intellectual property portfolio' and a proprietary mRNA platform (chemistry, delivery/LNP technology, manufacturing process science) built over years, plus regulatory approvals for three commercial products (Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE, mRESVIA) that competitors would need to replicate. However, the Risk Factors section also states Moderna competes against larger, better-resourced companies (Pfizer, Sanofi, GSK) that have exploited scale, bundling and purchasing power advantages, and that Moderna has been excluded from some European COVID sales due to a competitor's exclusive government contract, indicating the intangible-asset moat is real but not dominant or unchallenged.
red_flags: Total revenue fell 40% in 2025 ($1.9B vs $3.2B in 2024), driven by a 42% decline in net product sales, largely lower COVID vaccine demand
Company remains unprofitable, with a net loss of $2.8 billion in 2025 (though narrower than 2024's $3.6 billion loss)
Excerpts note exclusion from many European COVID vaccine markets due to a competitor's exclusive contract with the European Commission through year-end 2026
Prior FDA Refusal-to-File letter for the seasonal flu vaccine candidate required an amended BLA submission, showing regulatory execution risk
Company describes 'commercial challenges' in the RSV market due to more limited-than-expected ACIP recommendations

Heavy revenue concentration in COVID vaccines (COVID accounted for $1.81B of $1.818B total net product sales in 2025), with reliance on evolving regulatory/ACIP guidance and vaccination rate uncertainty
